description: This case study is the final report of the Buncefield Major Incident Investigation Board on the explosions and fire at the Buncefield oil storage and transfer depot in Hemel Hempstead, England, on the early morning of Sunday 11 December 2005. The Board, appointed by the Health and Safety Commission with an independent chair, Lord Newton of Braintree, contacted affected people and experts and reported progress publicly; this ninth and final report goes to the boards of the Health and Safety Executive and the Environment Agency, the joint competent authority. Volume 1 explains the significance of the depot, how the explosions and fires happened and the damage, and summarises all recommendations; Volume 2 brings together all the earlier reports in one publication. Access: free PDF of Volume 2 (208 pages) on the IChemE site; the page footer states the Open Government Licence v3.0. Coverage is one site and the regulation of major hazard fuel depots. Caveats: only the cover and introduction were read, and the tank overfill cause and casualty figures come from search summaries. It suits emergency response and hazard exposure studies of fuel storage terminals, and it relates to the HSE Buncefield response record catalogued here as case_study-buncefield-oil-depot-explosion-hse-response.

name: The Buncefield Incident 11 December 2005: final report of the Major Incident Investigation Board (fuel storage depot explosions and fire, UK)
outcomes: On the early morning of 11 December 2005 a series of explosions followed by a large fire destroyed large parts of the Buncefield oil storage and transfer depot and damaged homes and businesses around it. The Board's ninth and final report combines its earlier reports and summarises recommendations to regulators, industry and government on how the explosions and fires happened, the damage, and safety of fuel storage. Search-result summaries add that a tank overfilled after its safety equipment failed, over 40 people were injured with no fatalities, and damages were about one billion pounds.
